correctness.rationale: For 0<a,b<1 and every unitary U, diagonal covariance reduces U to one real rotation with t=|<1|U|0>|^2. The four composed Kraus operators give the normalized Choi partial-transpose determinant a^2[((1-a)^2(1-b)^2t^4)-b^2]/16, independently symbolically reconstructed and numerically spot-checked. A two-qubit partial transpose has at most one negative eigenvalue because every complex two-dimensional subspace contains a product vector, so the determinant sign decides PPT off the boundary; continuity proves equality. Choi separability and 2x2 PPT equivalence finish EB proof. The parameter orientation and edge cases were checked independently; finite tests are not proof of the universal implication.

value.rationale: Entanglement transmission through a cascade of two independently tuned nonunital damping stages is a physical scenario for which the exact set of admissible intermediate unitaries matters. The proof gives a sharp all-U decision criterion, an order-sensitive impossibility/possibility distinction at a natural rational pair, and the exact golden-ratio cutoff for matched stages. This is a continuous complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite example or a numerical reprint; it offers an interpretable design constraint beyond the known single-GAD criterion.
